title: Derived comparison of dg coefficient realizations with the normalized scheme arrow
statement:
Let $D\to E\to A$ be maps of commutative rings, let $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ be a separated finite type scheme, and put $Y_E=Y\times_D\operatorname{Spec}E$, $Y_A=Y\times_D\operatorname{Spec}A$, $p_E:Y_E\to Y$, $\pi_E:Y_A\to Y_E$, and $q_E:Y_E\to\operatorname{Spec}E$ [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions, def-pc-fibre-product]. Use the dg coefficient category, $\Phi_E$, $\widehat K$, $U$, and $\nu_E$ of [def-sfb-dg-coefficient-realization]. For $G\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{Y_E})$ and $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{Y_A})$ [def-pc-derived-category], there is a canonical isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_Y)$
$$U\Phi_E(G)\simeq Rp_{E*}\bigl(Lq_E^*\widetilde A\otimes^{\mathbf L}G\bigr).$$
Here $\widetilde A$ is the associated module on $\operatorname{Spec}E$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], and pullback and tensor are [def-pc-derived-pullback, def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. This isomorphism is natural in $G$, commutes with restriction to opens of $Y$, and identifies the actual arrow $U\nu_E(\gamma)$ with $Rp_{E*}\theta_{E,G,\gamma}$ for every $\gamma:G\to R\pi_{E*}K$. The arrow $\theta_{E,G,\gamma}$ is the adjoint [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint] of
$$L\pi_E^*(Lq_E^*\widetilde A\otimes^{\mathbf L}G)\simeq L(q_E\pi_E)^*\widetilde A\otimes^{\mathbf L}L\pi_E^*G\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{Y_A}\otimes^{\mathbf L}K\simeq K,$$
using the given scalar action and the transpose of $\gamma$. In particular $\Phi_E(G)$ and the cone of $\nu_E(\gamma)$ have quasi-coherent underlying cohomology. The comparison holds without flatness of $E\to A$ or $Y_E\to\operatorname{Spec}E$. For $E=D$, the functor $T=\Phi_D=\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}^{\mathbf L}-$ is left adjoint to $U$: for every $P\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ and $C\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal B)$ there is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal B)}(T(P),C)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_Y)}(P,UC)$, whose transpose is extension followed by the dg action. Forgetting actions preserves cones and their underlying cohomology. The category $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal B)$ with these cones is triangulated, $U$ is exact, and $T=\Phi_D$ is exact. On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}S\subseteq Y$ and for a finite polynomial surjection $Q=D[x_1,\ldots,x_r]\twoheadrightarrow S$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], restriction of dg actions along $Q\otimes_D R_A\to S\otimes_D R_A$, followed by the quasi-isomorphism equivalence $D(Q\otimes_D R_A)\simeq D(Q_A)$ induced by $Q\otimes_D R_A\to Q_A=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$, carries $\widehat K$ to the restriction of the affine $K$ to $Q_A$, carries $\Phi_D(P)$ to $Q_A\otimes_Q^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{Res}_Q^S P$, and carries their normalized arrows and cones to the corresponding scalar-action arrows and cones. More generally it carries $\Phi_E(G)$ to $Q_A\otimes_{Q_E}^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{Res}_{Q_E}^{S\otimes_D E}G$, with $Q_E=E[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$. Cohomology of these comparisons is the canonical $Q_A$-module cohomology, with its action factoring through $S\otimes_D A$ when the object is a $\mathcal B$-module.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal H_E=p_{E*}\mathcal O_{Y_E}$. The maps $p_E$ and $\pi_E$ are affine, being base changes of maps between affine spectra. Hence their direct images preserve quasi-coherent cohomology. The canonical map $g_E:(Y_E,\mathcal O_{Y_E})\to(Y,\mathcal H_E)$ gives an equivalence on quasi-coherent derived objects: take $L=Lg_E^*$ in the cited unit/counit theorem. Its inverse $Rg_{E*}$ identifies $Rp_{E*}G$ with a derived $\mathcal H_E$-module. This equivalence respects tensor and the specified adjunction maps: the tensor comparison for its right adjoint is inverse to the strong monoidal comparison for $Lg_E^*$, conjugated by its invertible unit and counit. Thus coefficient tensors and their action maps can be computed on $Y$ using $\mathcal H_E$-modules.

proof.text: Use the nonpositive termwise D-flat resolutions $R_E\to E$ and $R_A\to A$ specified in the current definition. They are D-K-flat by the bounded-above-flat theorem, so the existing left-module bar theorem applies with $P=R_E$, $Q=R_A$. Put $F_E=B(R_A,R_E,E)$. Each term is a direct sum of modules $R_A^i\otimes_D R_E^{j_1}\otimes_D\cdots\otimes_D R_E^{j_n}\otimes_D E$, with $i,j_k\leq0$ and bar shift $[n]$. Tensor products of flat D-modules are flat, their base changes to E are flat, and sums are flat: tensoring an exact sequence commutes with each of these operations. Thus $F_E$ is nonpositive and termwise E-flat, hence E-K-flat. By the symmetry for the commutative dg algebras, its underlying object represents $E\otimes_{R_E}^{\mathbf L}R_A$. The quasi-isomorphism $R_E\to E$ induces a derived equivalence; its unit at $R_A$ identifies $R_A$ with $\operatorname{Res}_{R_E}F_E$. The composite of this unit with the bar augmentation $F_E\to A$ is $R_A\to A$. The latter is a quasi-isomorphism, so $F_E\to A$ is one as well. This is an E-linear, E-K-flat resolution of A; no E-action on $R_A$ or flatness of E over D is asserted.

source.place: Tag 09S6 (dga.tex, lemma-qis-equivalence); Tag 0FTF and relative flat bar construction

proof.text: Put $M=Rg_{E*}G$, with its commuting $\mathcal O_Y$- and E-actions. Use the left bar convention of the current definition. In every bar degree the balancing map $$(R_A\otimes_D R_E^{\otimes_D n}\otimes_D E)\otimes_E M\longrightarrow R_A\otimes_D R_E^{\otimes_D n}\otimes_D M$$ sends $(h\otimes\mathbf r\otimes e)\otimes m$ to $h\otimes\mathbf r\otimes em$ and has inverse inserting $1\in E$. These maps respect the internal differential, all faces, the shifted left action and degeneracies. Hence $B(R_A,R_E,M)=F_E\otimes_E M$. Since $F_E$ is E-K-flat, this computes the derived coefficient tensor with its commuting structure-sheaf action. On each affine open of $Y$ the complex $F_E\otimes_E M$ is the tilde of the module total tensor, so it has quasi-coherent $\mathcal H_E$-cohomology and the unit of step 1 is invertible on it. Under the affine algebra equivalence of step 1 it is $Rp_{E*}(q_E^*\widetilde F_E\otimes G)$. The tilde tensor and affine pullback models identify $q_E^*\widetilde F_E$ with $Lq_E^*\widetilde A$. Its stalks are extensions of the E-K-flat complex $F_E$, hence K-flat by scalar extension and the stalk criterion. Thus the displayed tensor computes the derived tensor. This constructs the comparison globally through the affine algebra equivalence. The explicit balancing maps are natural and unchanged on open restrictions, as are the bar and pullback constructions.

Track $\gamma:G\to R\pi_{E*}K$ using the current definition's coefficient-linear direct images. The ringed-space composition theorem identifies $Rp_{E*}R\pi_{E*}K$ with $R\pi_{D*}K$ in $D(\mathcal H_E)$: use the two factorizations through $Y_E$ and through $(Y,\mathcal O_Y\otimes_D A)$. The final identity-space map is exact restriction, and the composites agree since $D\to E\to A$ commutes. Restriction along $R_E\to E$ retains this identification. By definition $\nu_E(\gamma)$ is the bar of $Rp_{E*}\gamma$ followed by the action counit. In left bar degree zero this sends $h\otimes m$ to $hm$, and in higher bar degrees it is zero, exactly as the cited bar theorem specifies. Under step 3 these maps are the augmentation $F_E\to A$ followed by the A-action on K. Its transpose along $L\pi_E^*\dashv R\pi_{E*}$ is therefore $L\pi_E^*Lq_E^*\widetilde A\otimes^{\mathbf L}L\pi_E^*G\to\mathcal O_{Y_A}\otimes^{\mathbf L}K\to K$, using that augmentation on the first factor and the transpose of $\gamma$ on the second. The monoidal pullback and composition comparisons identify its source and counit with those defining $\theta$. Adjunction and $Rp_{E*}$ now give $U\nu_E(\gamma)=Rp_{E*}\theta$. The natural global chain maps descend through quasi-isomorphism localization to arbitrary derived $\gamma$.

proof.text: Pullback and tensor preserve quasi-coherent cohomology, so the right side of the comparison has quasi-coherent cohomology after affine pushforward. Also $U\widehat K=R\pi_{D*}K$ has quasi-coherent cohomology. Forgetting the dg action leaves the underlying mapping cone unchanged. The quasi-coherent subcategory is closed under shifts and triangles (take the support subset to be all of Y in the cited supported-subcategory theorem). Thus the cone of $\nu_E(\gamma)$ is quasi-coherent as well. This also proves that the inherited triangles make $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal B)$ triangulated and that U restricts to an exact functor.

At E=D the constant resolution is D, so the defining tensor is $T(P)=\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}^{\mathbf L}P$. Apply the sheaf dg scalar adjunction to $\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal B$ (or opposite algebras for the left-module convention). Its right adjoint is exactly U, and its inverse Hom bijection is extension followed by the dg action counit. Both functors are exact. Step 5 shows T preserves the quasi-coherent subcategory, so this adjunction restricts to the full subcategories in the statement, without changing either Hom set or its transposition.

proof.text: On an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}S$, write $S_E=S\otimes_D E$ and represent G by its affine derived $S_E$-module M. Restriction from $S\otimes_D R_A$ to $Q\otimes_D R_A$ changes only the commuting algebra action on its bar model. Polynomial Q is D-free, so $Q\otimes_D R_A\to Q_A$ is a quasi-isomorphism; the cited dg equivalence carries the restricted bar to the Q_A object represented by coefficient extension of $\operatorname{Res}_{Q_E}^{S_E}M$. Choose a Q_E-K-flat replacement L of $\operatorname{Res}M$. It is E-K-flat: tensor an acyclic E-complex first with the E-free algebra Q_E and then with L. The augmentation $F_E\otimes_E L\to A\otimes_E L=Q_A\otimes_{Q_E}L$ is consequently a quasi-isomorphism, linear for $Q\otimes_D R_A$. Since $F_E$ is E-K-flat, $F_E\otimes_E L\to F_E\otimes_E M$ is also a quasi-isomorphism. This gives the asserted Q_A-object through the quasi-isomorphism equivalence, with the specified actions. For E=D this gives the stated formula for P. For $\widehat K$, all coefficient actions factor through the augmentation to A, so the same equivalence carries it to K restricted to Q_A. No assertion that $S\otimes_D R_A\to S\otimes_D A$ is a quasi-isomorphism is used.

proof.text: The polynomial calculation uses the same augmentation and action maps as step 4; restriction leaves them unchanged, and the dg equivalence carries the adjunction counit to the corresponding scalar-action map. Hence it carries the normalized arrows themselves, and exactness carries their triangles and cones. Finally $H^0(S\otimes_D R_A)=S\otimes_D A$: the complex is nonpositive, and right exactness of tensor identifies its degree-zero cokernel with $S\otimes_D H^0(R_A)$. Boundaries in degree zero act trivially on every module cohomology group, since $d(b)m=d(bm)$ for a cycle m. The action of $Q_A=H^0(Q\otimes_D R_A)$ on the compared cohomology is consequently the canonical one through $S\otimes_D A$. This proves the last clause, including the cone objects.
